html:
In 788 Idris ibn Abdallah, a great-grandson of the Prophet's grandson Hasan, was proclaimed leader by the Awraba Berbers at Volubilis. His state, the Idrisid dynasty, is counted as the first Moroccan state.

Idris had fled the Hejaz after a failed revolt against the Abbasid caliphs. In Morocco his descent from the Prophet gave him great prestige. He died in 791, by tradition poisoned by an agent of the caliph Harun al-Rashid. His son Idris II built Fez as the capital.

The Idrisid state broke up in the 900s, but it set a pattern: Morocco's later ruling families, the Saadis and today's Alaouites, also claimed descent from the Prophet. The tomb of Idris I at Moulay Idriss is one of Morocco's holiest places.
